FIND: `marker_match` (line 58–62) uses `ADMISSIBILITY\s*:?` with an **optional** colon. This means any line starting with the word "ADMISSIBILITY" in prose context — e.g., `ADMISSIBILITY gates fail under X conditions` inside a FIND or FOLLOW section — is accepted as the section header. Because ADMISSIBILITY is **not** in the `section_terminator` alternation (lines 81–83), there is no recovery path: the parser cannot re-anchor to the real `ADMISSIBILITY:` header. If any section terminator (FOLLOW, FIX, ANALYSE, etc.) appears between the false match and the real header, the extracted `block` contains only prose — no gate statuses — producing **false total failure on all 5 gates**.

File: `bench/logs/exp40_slice_admissibility_hardened_20260518T190104Z/working/_feedback_slice.py`, line 59.

Evidence — Python reproduction:
```
text = "FIND: problem\nADMISSIBILITY gates fail.\nFOLLOW: trace.\nADMISSIBILITY:\n  S_min: PASS\n..."
parse_admissibility_block(text) → ['S_min','G-completeness','d_tool','σ_measured','q_retest']
# Expected: [] (all gates pass)
```

FOLLOW: Every finding where a model mentions "ADMISSIBILITY" at the start of any line before the actual ADMISSIBILITY block (common in FIND/FOLLOW/ANALYSE sections that discuss admissibility requirements) will be flagged as total gate failure. The §17 feedback channel then tells the model to supply all 5 gates — for gates it already supplied correctly. This creates a feedback loop: the model re-emits the same block, the parser re-fails on the same false match, and the finding never closes. The feedback channel wastes cycles on a parser artefact, not a model deficiency. Downstream: inflated false-failure counts corrupt the ρ (discovery efficiency) metric.

ANALYSE: HARD constraint — the parser produces silently wrong results (all-gate failure when gates actually pass). This is correctness, not preference. The root cause is the optional colon `?` in `\s*:?` combined with the absence of ADMISSIBILITY from the section_terminator recovery list. CONFIRMED via tool-executed reproduction.

FIX: Make the colon mandatory in the marker regex. The prompt template (`cdsfl_operational.md` §15) explicitly shows `ADMISSIBILITY:` with a colon. Any model omitting the colon is already violating format; the parser should not weaken its anchor to accommodate a violation that creates a worse failure mode.
